label: copy-phase input w (fed-back w) in the middle of the copy
explanation: Token detector for w during the copy phase: 99% of activation mass is on copy-phase steps where the fed-back input is w (in_tok==w; this happens on about 10% of all copy-phase w inputs). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and almost never on other inputs (n is a distant second at 0.5% of mass). Position strongly gates it: there is no activation at recall_idx 0-1, it is weak at 2, and it peaks at recall_idx 3-4 (84% of mass), which means w was original token 2 or 3. It is suppressed when only 0-1 outputs remain, so it favours long sequences (L=8-9 holds 78% of mass) and the w sitting mid-copy. The largest activations (about 4.3) come from L=8-9 sequences where w is original token 2 or 3. Within a run like w w, the second w fires about half as strongly. Plain copy-phase w has recall 0.97 but precision 0.23. Adding the position window (recall_idx>=3, to_go>=2) gives dev F1 0.66 with mass recall 0.88. Many in-window w steps still stay silent, especially in shorter sequences, and the predicate does not capture this.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: w, n, c, v, x, 0; least: a, p, 3, q) and the token being output (most: n, 1, w, c, q, 0; least: b, p, 3, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, t=12.
